## Description

Primary source:

<https://ngs101.com/how-to-analyze-cell-cell-communication-in-single-cell-rna-seq-data-complete-beginners-guide-part-9-cellchat-analysis/>

Part 3 of 3. The CellChat objects for Healthy (part 1) and Post_Treatment
(part 2) are merged and compared: total interaction number and strength,
differential interactions between cell types, pathways whose total signaling
changes, outgoing and incoming signaling by cell type, ligand-receptor pairs
between selected cell types, and joint manifold learning to classify pathways
as shared or condition-specific. The article's "Common Pitfalls"
cell-type check on the two objects is run before the merge.

**Input.** `results/cellchat_Healthy.rds` (part 1) and
`results/cellchat_Post_Treatment.rds` (part 2) under
`<base.dir>/<cellchat.subdir>`. Parts 1 and 2 in turn need tutorial 7 part 1
to have been run (see their descriptions).

Code is taken from the source article's code blocks (steps 3.1-3.9 and the
cell-type check of its "Common Pitfalls" section). Changes made for this
notebook series: hard-coded values moved into the YAML front matter, paths built
from `params` rather than `setwd()`, and changes marked `ADDED:` or `FIX:` in
comments. Base-graphics plots are saved to PNG as in the article and shown in
the notebook with `knitr::include_graphics()`. `netEmbedding()` and
`netClustering()` are the slow steps.

## Libraries and directories

```{r step1_libs_data}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 1: Load required libraries
#-----------------------------------------------
library(CellChat)
library(patchwork)
library(ggplot2)
library(ComplexHeatmap) # netVisual_heatmap() returns ComplexHeatmap objects
library(reticulate)     # required by netEmbedding (Python UMAP via umap-learn)

if (!exists("params") || !is.list(params)) {
  # Running interactively (e.g. via "Run Cell") rather than through
  # knit/render, so `params` was never created by rmarkdown::render().
  # Reconstruct it by parsing this .Rmd's own YAML header, so the params
  # defaults live in exactly one place (the YAML block above) instead of
  # being duplicated here.
  rmd_path <- tryCatch(
    # Only reliable when this document is the active editor tab; if focus
    # has moved to another file, this will pick up the wrong path.
    rstudioapi::getSourceEditorContext()$path,
    error = function(e) NA_character_
  )
  if (is.na(rmd_path) || !nzchar(rmd_path)) {
    # Fallback if rstudioapi is unavailable or no doc is focused; assumes
    # the working directory is the project root.
    rmd_path <- "scRNAseq_tutorial_9_cell_communication_cellchat/tut9_cell_communication_cellchat_part3.Rmd"
  }
  params <- rmarkdown::yaml_front_matter(rmd_path)$params
}

# Set working directory
base.dir <- params$base.dir
cc.dir <- file.path(base.dir, params$cellchat.subdir)

# Set up the Python environment for netEmbedding().
# ADDED: wrapped in tryCatch so a Python/network problem does not stop the notebook;
# only netEmbedding() in Step 3.8 needs this environment.
tryCatch({
  virtualenv_create(params$reticulate.env)
  virtualenv_install(params$reticulate.env, packages = unlist(params$reticulate.packages))
  use_virtualenv(params$reticulate.env, required = TRUE)
}, error = function(e) {
  message("ADDED: Python environment setup failed (netEmbedding() in Step 3.8 will fail ",
          "unless umap-learn is available): ", conditionMessage(e))
})

options(stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Create output directories for all saved plots
plot.dir.comparison <- file.path(cc.dir, "plots/comparison")
dir.create(plot.dir.comparison, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

set.seed(params$seed)

# ADDED: show PNG files written by the base-graphics plots below in the notebook
show_png <- function(...) knitr::include_graphics(path.expand(c(...)))
```

## Load and merge the two CellChat objects

`mergeCellChat()` needs the same cell-type set in both objects. Part 1 removes
Healthy cell types with fewer than 10 cells (the article's pitfall check) and
part 2 does not, so the sets can differ; the article's cell-type check is
therefore run here before merging, and `liftCellChat()` is used only if the
sets differ.

```{r step3_1_merge}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 3.1: Load and Merge the Two CellChat Objects
#-----------------------------------------------
# Load saved objects (if starting fresh)
# ADDED: hand-off files from parts 1 and 2; stop with a clear message if missing
file.healthy <- file.path(cc.dir, "results/cellchat_Healthy.rds")
file.post <- file.path(cc.dir, "results/cellchat_Post_Treatment.rds")
stopifnot(file.exists(file.healthy), file.exists(file.post))
cellchat_healthy <- readRDS(file.healthy)
cellchat_post    <- readRDS(file.post)

# Check that cell type names match between conditions
# (article's "Common Pitfalls" check, moved here because mergeCellChat() needs it)
levels(cellchat_healthy@idents)
levels(cellchat_post@idents)
# They must be identical — both come from seurat_obj$final_annotation
# ADDED: if they differ, lift both objects to the union of cell types so that they can be merged
if (!identical(sort(levels(cellchat_healthy@idents)), sort(levels(cellchat_post@idents)))) {
  group.new <- union(levels(cellchat_healthy@idents), levels(cellchat_post@idents))
  message("ADDED: cell-type sets differ between conditions; lifting both objects to: ",
          paste(group.new, collapse = ", "))
  cellchat_healthy <- liftCellChat(cellchat_healthy, group.new)
  cellchat_post    <- liftCellChat(cellchat_post, group.new)
}
stopifnot(identical(sort(levels(cellchat_healthy@idents)), sort(levels(cellchat_post@idents))))

# Create a named list and merge
object.list <- list(
  cellchat_healthy,
  cellchat_post
)
names(object.list) <- c(params$healthy.level, params$post.level)

# Merge into a single CellChat object for comparative analysis
cellchat_merged <- mergeCellChat(
  object.list,
  add.names = names(object.list)
)
```

## Compare total interaction numbers and strength

```{r step3_2_compare_interactions}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 3.2: Compare Total Interaction Numbers and Strength
#-----------------------------------------------
gg1 <- compareInteractions(cellchat_merged, show.legend = FALSE, group = c(1, 2))
gg2 <- compareInteractions(cellchat_merged, show.legend = FALSE, group = c(1, 2), measure = "weight")
png(file.path(plot.dir.comparison, "01_interaction_count_vs_strength.png"), width = 1200, height = 750, res = params$plot.dpi)
print(gg1 + gg2)  # print() required to render patchwork inside png()/dev.off()
invisible(dev.off())
# ADDED: show the saved plot
show_png(file.path(plot.dir.comparison, "01_interaction_count_vs_strength.png"))
```

## Differential interactions as circle plots

```{r step3_3_circle_plots}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 3.3: Visualize Differential Interactions as Circle Plots
#-----------------------------------------------
circle_files <- character()  # ADDED: collect file names to show the plots afterwards
for (i in 1:length(object.list)) {
  fname <- file.path(plot.dir.comparison, paste0("02_circle_", tolower(names(object.list)[i]), ".png"))
  circle_files <- c(circle_files, fname)
  png(fname, width = 700, height = 700, res = params$plot.dpi)
  netVisual_circle(
    object.list[[i]]@net$count,
    weight.scale = TRUE, label.edge = FALSE,
    title.name   = paste("Number of Interactions -", names(object.list)[i])
  )
  invisible(dev.off())
}

# Red = increased in Post_Treatment; blue = decreased
png(file.path(plot.dir.comparison, "03a_diff_interactions_count.png"), width = 700, height = 700, res = params$plot.dpi)
netVisual_diffInteraction(cellchat_merged, weight.scale = TRUE)
invisible(dev.off())

png(file.path(plot.dir.comparison, "03b_diff_interactions_strength.png"), width = 700, height = 700, res = params$plot.dpi)
netVisual_diffInteraction(cellchat_merged, weight.scale = TRUE, measure = "weight")
invisible(dev.off())

# ADDED: show the saved plots
show_png(circle_files)
show_png(file.path(plot.dir.comparison, "03a_diff_interactions_count.png"))
show_png(file.path(plot.dir.comparison, "03b_diff_interactions_strength.png"))
```

## Compare pathway-level communication

```{r step3_5_ranknet}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 3.5: Compare Pathway-Level Communication
#-----------------------------------------------
# Information flow comparison — how does total signaling change per pathway?
# Bars show the total communication probability summed across all cell-type pairs
png(file.path(plot.dir.comparison, "05_rankNet_stacked.png"), width = 1050, height = 1200, res = params$plot.dpi)
rankNet(cellchat_merged, mode = "comparison", stacked = TRUE, do.stat = TRUE)
invisible(dev.off())

# Alternatively, view only pathways that change between conditions
png(file.path(plot.dir.comparison, "06_rankNet_sidebyside.png"), width = 1050, height = 1200, res = params$plot.dpi)
rankNet(cellchat_merged, mode = "comparison", stacked = FALSE)
invisible(dev.off())

# ADDED: show the saved plots
show_png(file.path(plot.dir.comparison, "05_rankNet_stacked.png"))
show_png(file.path(plot.dir.comparison, "06_rankNet_sidebyside.png"))
```

## Bubble plot and chord diagrams of specific cell-type pairs

```{r step3_7_bubble_chord}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 3.7: Bubble Plot of Specific Cell-Type Pair Interactions
#-----------------------------------------------
# ADDED: stop early if a cell type named in params is not in the objects
celltypes.all <- levels(object.list[[1]]@idents)
stopifnot(all(c(unlist(params$bubble.sources), unlist(params$bubble.targets),
                unlist(params$chord.sources), unlist(params$chord.targets)) %in% celltypes.all))

# Compare L-R interactions between Classical Monocytes (sender) and T cells (receiver)
png(file.path(plot.dir.comparison, "11_bubble_monocyte_to_Tcells.png"), width = 1500, height = 1200, res = params$plot.dpi)
netVisual_bubble(
  cellchat_merged,
  sources.use = unlist(params$bubble.sources),
  targets.use = unlist(params$bubble.targets),
  comparison  = c(1, 2),
  angle.x     = 45
)
invisible(dev.off())

# Chord diagram: L-R pairs from Classical Monocytes to CD4+ T cells — per condition
png(file.path(plot.dir.comparison, "12_chord_monocyte_CD4T_Healthy.png"), width = 1800, height = 1800, res = params$plot.dpi)
par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0))
netVisual_chord_gene(
  object.list[[1]],
  sources.use  = unlist(params$chord.sources),
  targets.use  = unlist(params$chord.targets),
  lab.cex      = params$chord.lab.cex,
  title.name   = paste0("Signaling from ", paste(unlist(params$chord.sources), collapse = ", "), " -- ", names(object.list)[1])
)
invisible(dev.off())

png(file.path(plot.dir.comparison, "13_chord_monocyte_CD4T_Post_Treatment.png"), width = 1800, height = 1800, res = params$plot.dpi)
par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0))
netVisual_chord_gene(
  object.list[[2]],
  sources.use  = unlist(params$chord.sources),
  targets.use  = unlist(params$chord.targets),
  lab.cex      = params$chord.lab.cex,
  title.name   = paste0("Signaling from ", paste(unlist(params$chord.sources), collapse = ", "), " -- ", names(object.list)[2])
)
invisible(dev.off())

# ADDED: show the saved plots
show_png(
  file.path(plot.dir.comparison, "11_bubble_monocyte_to_Tcells.png"),
  file.path(plot.dir.comparison, "12_chord_monocyte_CD4T_Healthy.png"),
  file.path(plot.dir.comparison, "13_chord_monocyte_CD4T_Post_Treatment.png")

```

## Joint manifold learning: shared and condition-specific pathways

`netEmbedding()` uses Python UMAP (umap-learn) through reticulate; see the
Python environment set up at the top of this notebook.

```{r step3_8_pairwise_embedding}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 3.8: Joint Manifold Learning: Classify Shared vs. Condition-Specific Pathways
#-----------------------------------------------
# Compute functional similarity between pathways across conditions
cellchat_merged <- computeNetSimilarityPairwise(cellchat_merged, type = "functional")
cellchat_merged <- netEmbedding(cellchat_merged, type = "functional")
options(future.rng.onMisuse = "ignore")
cellchat_merged <- netClustering(cellchat_merged, type = "functional")

# Visualize: pathways close together = functionally similar
# Pathways separated by condition = condition-specific
png(file.path(plot.dir.comparison, "14_pairwise_embedding.png"), width = 1200, height = 1050, res = params$plot.dpi)
netVisual_embeddingPairwise(cellchat_merged, type = "functional", label.size = 3.5)
invisible(dev.off())

png(file.path(plot.dir.comparison, "15_pairwise_embedding_zoom.png"), width = 1200, height = 1050, res = params$plot.dpi)
netVisual_embeddingPairwiseZoomIn(cellchat_merged, type = "functional", nCol = 2)
invisible(dev.off())

# ADDED: show the saved plots
show_png(file.path(plot.dir.comparison, "14_pairwise_embedding.png"))
show_png(file.path(plot.dir.comparison, "15_pairwise_embedding_zoom.png"))
```
